items.statement: Assume full AC. Let $F_+,F_-$ be compact smooth embedded spanning surfaces without closed components for the same nonempty nonsplit link $L\subset S^3$, with respectively positive and negative definite full rational normal-transfer pairings. They may be disconnected and nonorientable. Suppose their interior intersection is transverse and consists of finitely many embedded circles and properly ending embedded arcs, whose endpoints lie only on $L$, with a fixed boundary collar arrangement already supplied. Then an ambient isotopy of $F_+$ fixed near $L$ removes all interior circle components of its intersection with the original comparison surface $F_-$, while retaining its arc components and the boundary collar arrangement. Its full positive definite pairing is transported by the isotopy. The finite construction strictly reduces the circle count at each stage. The ambient isotopy need not fix the comparison surface pointwise; that surface is retained at its original position when intersections are measured.

citations.quote:
Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a nonempty compact smooth embedded surface, possibly disconnected and nonorientable, every component of which has nonempty boundary. The ambient sphere has its standard orientation. The normal-transfer expression $B_F([a],[b])=\operatorname{lk}(a,\tau b)$ defines a symmetric integral bilinear pairing on the free finite-rank group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, with rational extension. It restricts on each component to its normal-transfer pairing; for cycles $a,b$ on distinct components its value is $2\operatorname{lk}(a,b)$, which need not vanish.

Suppose an embedded product cylinder $W=[-1,1]\times D^2$ meets $F$ exactly in its two end disks, on distinct components. Replace those disks by the lateral annulus and round the seams to obtain $F'$. There is an integral basis in which $B_{F'}$ has matrix $G\oplus[0]$, where $G$ is the entire matrix of $B_F$, including its cross-component entries. Thus its signature is unchanged. The boundary link and its surface collar remain fixed, so $e(F)=-\sum_i\operatorname{lk}(K_i,K_i')$, computed from boundary normal push-offs, is unchanged as well.

A finite sequence of such tubes exists making $F$ connected. All intermediate surfaces still have the original boundary link and collar, no closed components, and finite smooth disk-and-band presentations on their components. The signature and $e$ are preserved throughout.

Assume full AC. Let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth embedded surface with nonempty boundary, possibly nonorientable, with a supplied finite smooth disk-and-band presentation. The ambient three-sphere has its standard orientation. For oriented integral multicurves $a,b\subset\operatorname{int}F$, let $\tau b$ be the cycle consisting of the two small normal pushes over $b$, oriented by projection to $b$. For a one-sided circle this is one circle mapping with degree two, rather than a choice of a single normal direction. Then
$B_F([a],[b])=\operatorname{lk}(a,\tau b)$ defines a well-defined symmetric integral bilinear pairing on $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, independently of representatives and sufficiently small normal pushes. Every integral homology class has an oriented multicurve representative, permitting integer coefficients. The pairing extends to rational homology, with quadratic form $q_F(x)=B_F(x,x)$ satisfying the normal-transfer linking identity.

For an embedded compact subsurface $A\subset F$ with such a finite presentation, the pairing on $A$ is the pullback of $B_F$ under inclusion. If $F$ is oriented and its boundary is one knot, its pairing has matrix $V+V^T$ in any integral basis, where $V$ is the positive-push Seifert matrix. Orientation-preserving ambient isotopies transport the pairing.

Assume full AC. Let $F_+,F_-$ be connected compact smooth surfaces embedded in the oriented standard three-sphere, each with nonempty boundary and possibly nonorientable. Supply quadratic forms $q_\pm$ on $H_1(F_\pm;\mathbb Q)$, positive definite and negative definite respectively. Suppose that for every oriented rational multicurve $c$ in the interior of the corresponding surface, $q_\pm[c]=\operatorname{lk}(c,\tau_\pm c)$. Here $\tau_\pm c$ is the cycle obtained by pushing the two-sheeted unit normal line cover of $c$ a sufficiently small distance off that surface, with both sheets oriented by projection to $c$; linking is extended bilinearly over rational coefficients. Let $\gamma$ be a smooth embedded circle in both interiors, and assume their tangent planes are transverse along $\gamma$. Then $\gamma$ bounds a smooth embedded disk in each of $F_+$ and $F_-$. Zero-dimensional first homology is allowed in the definiteness assumptions. The statement makes no assertion that the two disk interiors are mutually disjoint.
An oriented link $L\subset S^3$ is **split** if a smoothly embedded sphere $S\subset S^3\setminus L$ has link points in both components of $S^3\setminus S$; otherwise $L$ is **nonsplit**.

Assume countable choice. Let $S\subset S^3$ be the image of a smooth embedding of the standard $S^2$. There is a smooth ambient isotopy $H_t:S^3\to S^3$, with $H_0=\operatorname{id}$, such that $H_1(S)$ is the standard equatorial sphere $E$. In particular $S^3\setminus S$ has exactly two components. Their closures $B_+$ and $B_-$ are smoothly embedded standard closed $3$-balls with common boundary $S$. If $D_+$ and $D_-$ denote the standard closed hemispheres bounded by $E$, the labels can be chosen so that the restrictions $H_1:B_\pm\to D_\pm$ are diffeomorphisms with the same boundary restriction $H_1|_S:S\to E$. Thus the ball identifications are compatible on their boundary and on a common two-sided collar of that boundary.

Assume countable choice. For $n=2$ or $3$, a smoothly embedded closed $n$-ball in a connected boundaryless smooth $n$-manifold can be carried to a sufficiently small coordinate round ball by a smooth ambient isotopy. Consequently, a smooth closed disk in the boundary of a smooth $3$-ball is a standard disk window: the pair consisting of the ball and that disk is diffeomorphic to a round ball with a hemispherical boundary disk. Attaching a smooth $3$-ball to a smooth manifold along one such disk window does not change the diffeomorphism type, after smoothing the corner. The same conclusion holds in reverse, when a ball meeting the boundary in one disk is removed; the diffeomorphism is supported near the attached or removed ball and its attaching collar.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$.

1. **Compact main case.** Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold, possibly with boundary, let $N$ be a smooth manifold without boundary, let $F:M\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings that is constant near the ends of $I$, and let $W$ be an open neighbourhood of $F(M\times I)$ in $N$. Then there is an ambient isotopy $H:N\times I\to N$ with $H_0=\mathrm{id}_N$, every $H_t$ a diffeomorphism, $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ for all $t\in I$, $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ outside $W$ for every $t$, and $H_t$ stationary near the ends; if $F$ is constant near the ends with parameter $\varepsilon$, then $H_t=\mathrm{id}_N$ for $t\le\varepsilon/2$ and $H_t=H_1$ for $t\ge1-\varepsilon/2$.
2. **Relative form.** Let $N$ be boundaryless, $U\subseteq N$ open, $A\subseteq U$ compact, and let $F:U\times I\to N$ be a smooth isotopy of embeddings whose track image is open in $N\times I$. Then there is a compactly supported ambient isotopy $H$ of $N$ with $H_t\circ F_0=F_t$ on a neighbourhood of $A$ for every $t$.
3. **Boundary stratum.** If $N$ has boundary and $F(M\times I)\subseteq\partial N$, then the ambient isotopy of clause 1 can be chosen with every $H_t$ carrying $\partial N$ onto itself; if $F(M\times I)\subseteq N\setminus\partial N$, it can be chosen compactly supported in $N\setminus\partial N$.
4. **General isotopies.** For the same compact source (possibly with boundary) and boundaryless target as in clause 1, every smooth isotopy extends with support in a compact subset of any prescribed neighbourhood $W$ of $F(M\times I)$. The endpoint-constancy hypothesis and the stationary-end conclusion are both omitted; all other conclusions of clause 1 hold.

derivations.claim: The first homology of a connected component injects as its summand in that of the disjoint union. Therefore the restriction of the positive or negative definite full pairing to each component is still definite of that sign. By [F1] a common transverse interior circle consequently bounds a disk on both its containing components, without needing their boundary links to agree. If no circle is present use the identity isotopy. Otherwise choose a common circle $\gamma$ whose disk $D_-$ in $F_-$ is innermost among the finitely many such disks. Its interior contains no other common circle. It contains no intersection arc either: the endpoints of an arc lie on $L$ outside this interior disk, so an arc entering it would have to cross $\gamma$, whereas distinct transverse intersection components are disjoint. Thus $\operatorname{int}D_-\cap F_+=\varnothing$. Let $D_+\subset F_+$ be the disk supplied by [F1]. The same endpoint argument shows no intersection arc enters $D_+$.

The two disks have disjoint interiors, since $\operatorname{int}D_-$ misses the whole of $F_+$. Perform two-copy disk surgery on $F_+$ along $D_-$, cutting out a thin annulus at $\gamma$, capping its two sides by nearby copies of $D_-$, and smoothing the seams in their transverse disk charts. This splits off a smooth sphere $S_0$ made from $D_+$ and one cap; the rest is a surface $F_1$ obtained from the one affected component by replacing its disk. That component stays connected and retains its original nonempty boundary, and every other component of $F_+$ is retained. Thus $F_1$ has no closed components and boundary exactly $L$. Choose the new cap of $F_1$ on the side of $F_-$ occupied by the retained part near $\gamma$, rounding its seam to that same side. It and its seam then miss $F_-$. The two-copy surgery makes $S_0$ disjoint from the whole $F_1$ and from $L$. Its sphere smoothing and all caps may be chosen arbitrarily close to the original disks, with no other intersection changed outside the discarded disk.

By [F3] the sphere $S_0$ has two ball sides. Because $L$ is nonsplit and disjoint from it, [F2] implies all of $L$ lies on one side. Every component of $F_1$ lies entirely on one side, since it is connected and disjoint from $S_0$. It has nonempty boundary contained in $L$, so it must lie on the side containing $L$. Consequently the opposite ball $V$ misses the entire $F_1$ and $L$, not just the affected component. Reverse the two-copy surgery by joining $S_0$ to $F_1$ through their short original product collar. Absorb this collar into $V$ by [F4]. The resulting ball $V'$ meets $F_1$ in exactly one disk window and has interior disjoint from $F_1$ and $L$. Replacing that window by its other boundary disk recovers the original $F_+$ up to the arbitrarily small seam choices of step 2.1. This is where nonsplitting replaces a connectedness assumption on the entire spanning surface.

In the ball-window coordinates of [F4], flatten the window cap and shrink the other cap in its normal coordinate. After smoothing its edge the bulged disk is a graph $t=g(x)$, $g\ge0$ smooth and zero on a boundary collar, while the window is $t=0$. The graph interpolation $t=(1-u)g(x)$ removes this bulge through embedded disks fixed on that collar. Extend by the identity on the rest of the surface and make it stationary near the time endpoints. Its compact track has a neighborhood missing $L$ and every other component and missing the retained surface outside the fixed collar. Apply [F5] there to obtain an ambient isotopy carrying $F_+$ to $F_1$ and fixed near $L$. Hence the endpoint pairing is the transported full pairing by [F1], including all cross-component terms. There is no requirement to avoid the comparison surface during the isotopy.

At the endpoint the new cap and seam miss $F_-$ by step 2.1. The circle $\gamma$ and any circles inside $D_+$ are gone, all other intersection components outside that disk are retained, and no arc has changed by step 1.1. Thus the finite circle count strictly decreases. The retained transverse family and unchanged collar arrangement satisfy the hypotheses again, so repeat the construction until that count is zero. A decreasing nonnegative integer permits at most the original number of stages. Concatenate the finitely many isotopies; their finite common fixed neighborhood is still a neighborhood of $L$. This proves every asserted relative and endpoint property without assuming the initial surfaces connected.

boundaries.reason: A nonempty boundary link and spanning surfaces without closed components are assumed.

boundaries.evidence: The Statement allows zero first Betti number and zero signature; no inverse of the normal form is taken.
The Statement allows a one-component link and connected or disconnected surfaces satisfy the same argument.
The Statement uses the signature, which is the difference of positive and negative ranks; the proof does not require nonsingularity.
The Statement retains the same literal boundary link, with arbitrary component orientations.
The Statement explicitly assumes full AC, which is assumed and inherited through the cited linking and smooth construction suppliers.

axioms.use: Full AC is inherited from the opposite-definite common-circle and full normal-transfer pairing suppliers. It supplies countable choice for smooth Schoenflies, ball-window normalization and compact supported isotopy extension. All circle reductions are finite.
